name: cloud-drive
description: Diego's Cloud Drive — standalone Android storage app, lifted out of the SuperApp's Cloud▸Apps▸Drive pages so the phone's storage surface is its own icon. #579 NATIVE COMPOSE CHROME (the WebView page and its string-named bridge are gone): a five-tab shell drawn by the fleet's bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav) — Files, Apps, Sync, Backups, Configs — every tab, sub-page, place, filter and icon name declared in ui.* below and baked through BuildConfig. Files is a FULL X-plore-class manager over shared storage: two real panes with their own tabs, collapsible tree view, archives browsed as folders, copy/move between panes with live progress, multi-select action bar, bookmarks, breadcrumbs, sort/filter, storage bar, the shared store (storage.shared_root) first. Sync ▸ Git is GitSync-class: one card per managed repository with live branch / ahead-behind / dirty / conflicts and the last sync, one-tap sync with stepped progress, per-repo period / network rule / auth, a persisted sync history, conflicts surfaced. Sync ▸ Rclone and ▸ Mounts use the same card language over libs:rclone and libs:mounts; Apps is a grid of the fleet's data apps (data/drive-apps.json resolved against the constellation manifest, #437); Backups runs the declared mirror (rsync) jobs with cancellable progress; Configs holds the app's settings. The four engine libraries (#567) and the ONE shared store (#575) are unchanged underneath. Dark is the default theme, set at the declaration (#336, #337). Design: a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-drive-redesign.md. The PDF reader is the #577 native pdfium engine (build.json::pdf), the fleet's one in-process renderer, opened from the Files tab and from any app's Open-with. Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.
_doc_rsync: TASK #330 named Rsync without naming a home. It lives INSIDE the Backups tab, because a one-way folder copy with rsync's size-plus-mtime quick check IS the 'on-device backup set' that tab was already declared to hold, and a fifth tab for one list of jobs would have split the same subject across two screens. The jobs are declared in data/drive-mirror-jobs.json and executed by FilesBridge.mirror(). EVERY DESTINATION IS ON-DEVICE and no fleet host is addressed: see that file's _doc_fleet_destination for why (an APK cannot hold the credential), and rep-N2.md for what that defers.

android._doc_packaging_excludes: Duplicate META-INF files that must not reach the APK. #567 push 2 links libs:git-sync, which pulls JGit, jsch and their notices; two jars carrying the same META-INF/LICENSE fail mergeDebugJavaResource for the WHOLE app. Same block, same reason and same list as ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/build.json, which packages these very modules 36 times over. Data, not gradle, so the next collision is a one-line edit here. Never add *.kotlin_module: dropping those breaks Kotlin reflection at runtime, silently. META-INF/versions/*/OSGI-INF/MANIFEST.MF (a glob, every multi-release level): the mwiede jsch fork ships an OSGi manifest under versions/9 AND versions/15, and so do jspecify (9) and bouncycastle via sshj (15) — measured on runs 36068993994 and 36074399160, 2026-09-24. One level at a time was a chase.

storage._doc: #575 THE ONE DECLARATION of the on-phone repo store. cloud-drive is THE store: every clone the git manager makes and every phone-side leg of an rclone job lives under <shared storage>/<shared_root>/<name>, in plain shared storage, so every fleet app that holds all-files access reads AND writes it the way it reads /storage/emulated/0 — no per-app clone, no Android/data sandbox. RELATIVE TO SHARED STORAGE on purpose: the absolute form (/storage/emulated/0/...) is a fact about one device — the user id in it changes under a second profile (drive-mirror-jobs.json _doc_paths states the same rule). Consumers: app/build.gradle bakes it into BuildConfig.SHARED_ROOT (SharedStore.kt resolves it at runtime); ac_cloud-code/tools/resolve-targets.py READS it from this file at build time so cloud-code's Backlog and Repos tabs point at the same folder without restating it. test/test-drive-shared-store.sh fails the build on a second copy of the value or an absolute path anywhere.

git_sync._doc: Scheduled background sync of the repositories the user opted in (ManagedRepo.autoSync), the GitSync app's scheduler realised over WorkManager (GitSyncWorker.kt). interval_minutes is the period (WorkManager's floor is 15); require_unmetered_network keeps a push off mobile data. Same shape and same reason as release.auto_update: a build.json edit reaches installed phones through ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE on the next launch.

ui._doc: #579 THE STRUCTURE OF THE CHROME, declared. Kotlin holds no tab list, no caption, no place list and no icon name: DriveShell renders ui.tabs, SyncScreen renders ui.sync.pages, the Files Places sheet renders ui.files.places, the Files filter pills render ui.files.filters. Every `icon` here is a name IconCatalog.kt resolves to a Material glyph; a name it does not know renders ui.icons._default and test/test-drive-shell.sh fails the build. Baked by app/build.gradle as UI_TABS_B64 / UI_SYNC_B64 / UI_FILES_B64 / UI_ICON_DEFAULT and decoded ONCE by Declarations.kt.

sync._doc: The strip inside the Sync island. git_periods_minutes are the per-repository period choices the repo Settings sheet offers (ManagedRepo.syncIntervalMinutes); 0 is never offered here because 0 means 'the base period storage.git_sync.interval_minutes'. Every value is at or above WorkManager's 15-minute floor.

files._doc_places: The Places sheet, in order. kind: shared_root = storage.shared_root under shared storage (ALWAYS first, hero); external_root = shared storage itself; public_dir = Environment.DIRECTORY_<dir> under it; external_path = a relative path under it. A place whose folder does not exist on the device is not offered. Removable volumes, the app's slice on them and the SAF grant are discovered at runtime, not declared. The store's label is 'Shared store', never the application's name: the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) refuses any label that spells an app name the old way.
files._doc_filters: The filter pills of a pane. An entry matches by mime (exact), mime_prefix, or extensions (lower-case, no dot); `all` has no rule and matches everything. Folders always pass a filter so the tree stays walkable.

icons._doc: The glyph an unknown icon name renders. IconCatalog knows this name too.

pdf._doc: #577 THE ONE PDF ENGINE declaration. cloud-drive is the fleet's PDF reader (#458) and its reader is the only in-process PDF renderer in the fleet (#463): every other app reaches it through the Android manifest (an ACTION_VIEW application/pdf chooser), never by carrying a renderer. app/build.gradle reads this block and adds the dependency, so the pin lives in data, not in a gradle string; test/test-drive-pdf-engine.sh holds the app's source to it (the only file that names the library is PdfEngine.kt).

engine._doc_artifacts: BOTH, on the compile classpath. The binding's Gradle metadata publishes pdfiumandroid-core (the JNI half, where the .so files live) as a RUNTIME-only dependency, but the public constructor PdfiumCore(context, config, coreInternal: PdfiumCoreU = ...) names a class from it, so the Kotlin compiler cannot compile a bare PdfiumCore(context) without it (found reading pdfiumandroid-2.0.0.module and PdfiumCore.kt, not by building: there is no build here). pdfiumandroid-api (models, FindFlags, PdfPasswordException) arrives transitively.
engine._doc_version: PINNED ON PURPOSE BELOW THE LATEST (2.0.3, 3.0.x-alpha). 2.0.1 and later publish against kotlin-stdlib 2.4, and this repo compiles with Kotlin 2.3.20 (root build.gradle): a Kotlin compiler reads class metadata one minor version ahead at most, so 2.0.1+ would fail to compile here. 2.0.0 is a stable release built with Kotlin 2.3.10, read from the sources jar and the AARs on Maven Central, not from memory. Raise it together with the root Kotlin plugin version, never alone.
engine._doc_licence: The binding is Apache-2.0 (its LICENSE; the pom declares the same). The native engine inside it, PDFium, is BSD-3-Clause (pdfium.googlesource.com LICENSE). Both permissive: nothing copyleft reaches the APK and nothing is vendored into this repository, which is what 1_cicd/src/data/licence-boundaries.json guards (mixed-licence upstreams whose restricted directories must stay out). It is a Maven Central dependency, not a source tree.
engine._doc_native_abis: What the AAR ships (libpdfium.so + libpdfiumandroid.so per ABI, ~5 MB for arm64-v8a). android.abi_filters still decides which of them reach an APK.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A0_keys/providers/android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A0_keys/providers/android/signing.secrets.yaml.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:ml-l-image-mlkit._doc_dir: THE shared scan engine (task #459/#460): ZXing barcode decode + ML Kit text-recognition + typed-payload parsing, shared BY REFERENCE the same way libs:core and libs:updater are. cloud-media-center consumes the SAME directory — one engine, two apps, no private copy to drift.

modules._doc_engines: #567 THE FOUR ENGINE LIBRARIES. The owner's vision for this application: the main APK is CHROME, and every tooling is a full engine in its OWN library — libs:file-editor (the full text editor), libs:git-sync (the native git manager that finishes the #437/#448 GitSync story: status, stage/unstage, commit, push/pull, branch list, log, diff, remotes, conflicts — GitSync's UX, over JGit), libs:rclone (remotes config + declared/ad-hoc sync jobs with progress + remote browsing, over a sha256-pinned static rclone binary) and libs:mounts (ftp/sftp/ssh/webdav connections with browse-through). Each lives on the shared shelf and is shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here, so lib-apks also ships each one as cloud-lib-{name}. THE MODULE BOUNDARY IS LAW: a library imports nothing from any application (test/test-drive-engine-modules.sh fails on the first lib -> app import). Compose only (#565): each exports ONE @Composable screen that this app's EngineActivity hosts (push 5). Landed as independently green pushes — (1) skeletons + declarations, (2) git-sync, (3) file-editor, (4) rclone + mounts, (5) drive wiring — so a module on main is never half-wired: until its engine push lands, a skeleton renders its own title and nothing else, and the app does not route to it.

libs:git-sync._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 2: the native git manager. Lives on the shelf beside the vendored Flutter GitSync tree (libs/gitsync, GPL-3.0) whose UI could not be embedded; this module is the Kotlin/Compose realisation of that UX over JGit.

libs:file-editor._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 3: the full text editor that replaces the in-page textarea editor of #302 for anything beyond a quick edit.

libs:rclone._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 4: rclone remotes + jobs + progress. The declared jobs stay in this app's data/drive-rclone-jobs.json and data/drive-remotes.json; the library receives them as models, never reads them itself.

libs:mounts._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 4: ftp / sftp / ssh / webdav mounts with browse-through. Declared fleet connections stay in data/drive-connections.json; the library receives them as models.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: #579 THE fleet bottom-nav island (#565): the five tabs are drawn by the same Compose declaration superapp, mail, wallet and me render — one geometry, one pill, one collapse rule. Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here.

modules._doc_engine_flag: #579 `engine: true` marks a module as one of the FOUR ENGINE LIBRARIES (the host contract: one @Composable <X>Screen(target, onOpenFile, onClose), a title string, the module boundary). Until #579 every Compose library this app linked WAS an engine, so test-drive-engine-modules.sh discovered engines as 'Compose library'; libs:bottomnav (the fleet's nav island, chrome not tooling) is the first Compose library here that is not one, so the role is now declared, not inferred.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. Until #330 this block was absent and test/ did not exist, so the shell phase printed COVERAGE-GAP and exited 0: the only question this application's pipeline asked was whether Gradle exited 0, and Gradle cannot see a WebView calling a Kotlin class by string name.

shell._doc_requires: A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail — it returns a verdict from the tool's ABSENCE. Listing them here makes a missing one fatal at the engine's preflight instead of a green tick over assertions that never ran.

unit._doc: Runs gradle test (build.sh test — the app's documented 'gradle test (JVM unit tests)' step) on every ship. #579 the app module now carries its own JVM suite (app/src/test: the Files state reducers, the archive path model, the transfer/rename plans, the Zip-Slip guard, the sync history and the per-repo schedule decision, the declarations, and a Robolectric Compose layout-tree test of the shell and the Files pane). The module graph also includes :libs:ml-l-image-mlkit, whose typed-payload parser suite lives in this app's unit phase on purpose, and the four engine libraries' suites. #577 adds PdfConvertTest and PdfLayoutTest, which run the PDF converter and the reader's page layout as real code on the CI runner.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.
